title: Monte Carlo uncertainty is a hard-coded flat +/-15% band on zero live rows, and the 9999 clamp makes it understate an elite asset by 5.07%
claimUnderTest: monte_carlo.py module docstring: 'Given side-A and side-B as lists of players, each with a valueBand from Phase 4 (p10, p50, p90)... Depends on: Phase 4 confidence intervals'. build_trade_player: 'Prefers the Phase 4 valueBand dict; falls back to +/-15% band'.
observed: 0 of 1,092 playersArray rows carry a valueBand, so the fallback IS the production path for every asset — every player, pick and defender is drawn from an identical +/-15% triangle regardless of whether the board blended 1 source or 14 (effectiveSourceRanks ranges 0-14 across the contract). The frontend synthesizes the same +/-15% band client-side. Worse, _shifted() clamps to 9999 while the +15% leg is not, so for a top-of-board asset the upper half of the band is truncated and the sampled mean falls BELOW the board value: Brock Bowers (rankDerivedValue 9947) simulates at sideAMean 9441.9. No convergence diagnostic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned; ten identical calls give winProbA 0.0001-0.0003 and meanDelta -4455.2 to -4439.3.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('rows with valueBand:',sum(1 for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('valueBand')),'of',len(d['playersArray']))" ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["sideAMean"], r["nSims"])'
reproduction.expected: sideAMean == 9947 (the board value the user is shown)

numericProof.formula: E[draw] = sum over segments of ((lo+hi)/2)*weight, using the piecewise-linear _triangular_draw quantile map

userImpact: On /trade the MC panel says 'Side B came out ahead in 100% of 20,000 simulations'. That number is produced from an invented, uniform uncertainty and a mean that is 5% low for exactly the elite assets a trade usually hinges on. A user rejects an even trade because the simulator's fabricated distribution says it is not close.

priorFinding.note: Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F03 and PRIOR-A10-F02, which state the same defect from the constants and documentation angles. New here is the 9999-clamp bias: the fabricated band is not merely uninformative, it is directionally WRONG at the top of the board, understating the board value by 504 points (5.07%) with an analytic derivation that matches the live sideAMean to 1.1 points.

whatWorks: The direction-symmetrization is real and effective (symmetryCheck.drift 0.0001, enforced true), the labelHint/disclaimer contract fields ARE returned by the backend, and run-to-run variance is genuinely small (meanDelta sd 5.1 on a magnitude of 4,447 over 10 runs at 100k sims) — the estimator is stable, it is just estimating a fabricated quantity.
rootCause: The band producer (src/canonical/confidence_intervals) never stamps valueBand onto contract rows, so the documented input does not exist on any live row; the fallback was written as a degradation path and became the only path.
requiredRepair: Either stamp valueBand from the data the contract already carries (effectiveSourceRanks spread / sourceSpread / confidenceBucket are all present per row), or stop reporting a win probability and report the point delta only. At minimum, clamp p50 and p90 consistently so the sampled mean equals the displayed board value, and return a convergence statistic (MC standard error on winProbA) so the reader can tell a stable 0.50 from a noisy one.
dependencies: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py has no producer wired into the contract build.
